root_cause.text: In `acpi_processor_errata_piix4()`, device pointers `ide_dev` and `isa_dev` were dereferenced in `dev_dbg()` calls after `pci_dev_put()` dropped their reference count, causing a use-after-free, and debug messages were printed even when the corresponding errata flags were not set.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states "device pointers may be dereferenced after dropping references to the device objects pointed to by them, which may cause a use-after-free." The patch moves the `dev_dbg()` calls to before the `pci_dev_put()` calls and inside the conditionals that set the errata flags, ensuring the pointers are valid when accessed and messages only appear when the errata is actually enabled.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix debug message for Type-F DMA livelock erratum to only print when the erratum is detected, and remove misplaced BM-IDE debug message.
intent_record.what: Moved the dev_dbg call for 'Type-F DMA livelock erratum (C3 disabled)' from after the switch block to inside the if condition that sets errata.piix4.fdma = 1, and removed the separate dev_dbg call for 'Bus master activity detection (BM-IDE) erratum enabled' that was printed after the switch. Also added curly braces to the if block.
intent_record.how: Previously, the Type-F erratum debug message was printed unconditionally after the switch; now it is printed only when the corresponding bit is set, providing accurate runtime diagnostics. The BM-IDE debug message is no longer emitted from this location, likely moved or deemed unnecessary.
